Prasidh to Chahar, FOUR runs 
Chahar finishes with a flourish, and MI will have 155 to defend! Banged into the track 
on leg stump, Chahar gives himself plenty of room and slugs it to long on's right. A 
boundary to end the innings and the crowd, even if momentarily, does find its voice! 
Rashid Khan: (On if he is back to his best) 70-75%, I would say. Wherever I have given 
runs, it is about the length and that is something I had in my mind. I wanted to hit the 
right areas. The hardest part is when you are having the rehab, those 3-4 months, when 
you are trying to bowl not in full rhythm, you just get used to a different landing, different 
follow-through and everything. Getting back…I feel I am 80% there. I do analyse myself a 
lot. Just about taking that (surgery) out of my mind and bowl how I was bowling before 
that. (On the pitch) There is something for the spinners, but you have to hit the right 
areas consistently. The way Sai mixed up his pace and bowled his variations, that is 
something that put us back in the game. I feel this wicket is helpful, you have to hit the 
right areas. We need to play good cricket, like we have been so far, and making sure 
whoever goes in there takes responsibility (and finishes the job). 
MI, on the other hand, will feel they have left a few runs out there. A lot of their batters 
perished to attacking strokes and that might be called into question, given the game 
situation. Jacks and Suryakumar looked comfortable at the crease, but that was about it 
from a batting perspective. Vishal tells me a few dew ropes and super soppers are 
going around the field, which indicates the presence of dew, and if that is the case, MI 
will have their task cut out defending this score. Join us in a bit for the chase! 
9:23pm An exceptional bowling display by the Titans, and how often have they done it 
this season. Restricting this MI batting unit to 155 was commendable, and it could have 
been even better had the Titans held on to the chances that came their way during the 
powerplay. But like all champion sides, they put that disappointment behind them, with 
Rashid and Sai Kishore calling the shots through the middle. Prasidh was expensive in 
his first and fourth overs, but in between, bowled two overs for just three runs (and a 
wicket), with Coetzee also impressing. Arshad, with the new ball, was also pretty 
effective.
